concept.name: Full fill
concept.definition: An execution (or series of executions) that completes the entire quantity of an order, leaving nothing open. Once fully filled, the order is terminal - it can no longer be canceled or modified.
concept.intuition: The order got every share it asked for; nothing remains in the market.
concept.mechanics: The venue reports a final execution bringing cumulative quantity to the full order quantity; in FIX this is OrdStatus = Filled ('order completely filled, no remaining quantity') with LeavesQty = 0. A full fill may result from one execution or the accumulation of many partial fills.
concept.formula: Full fill condition: CumQty = OrderQty and LeavesQty = 0.
concept.failure_modes: A full fill at a stale price can itself be the failure - e.g., a resting order that completes only because the market blew through its level (adverse selection in disguise). Confirmed full fills also cannot be unwound except by error-correction procedures.
concept.misconceptions: Full fill says nothing about price quality - an order can be completely filled at several progressively worse prices. And 'filled' does not mean settled; clearing and settlement follow execution.
concept.example: Your 5,000-share buy at $30 executes in three partials of 2,000, 2,000, and 1,000; the last report shows CumQty 5,000, LeavesQty 0, OrdStatus Filled.

citations.source: FIX 4.2 Execution Report (MsgType 8), FIX Dictionary (Onix Solutions)
